note: Table row 'Governors, governors-general, viceroys, residents, high commissioners': not a reign (representative); the office is another state's, exercised on its behalf (office test).
Table row 'Consorts': not a reign, unless the lead or succession shows rule in her own right (a verdict ruling by uuid).
Table row 'Consorts', read from the evidence record: a consort category and a consort lead, and no category of this row's monarchs.
Table row 'Co-rulers': a junior named and never exercising (Caesar, heir, crown prince, designate) is not a reign.
Table row 'Collective heads of state': the chair is the reign; members are other office (Bosnia's Presidency).
Table rows 'Co-rulers' and 'Collective heads': each Captain Regent of San Marino and each Co-Prince of Andorra is a spell of a holder who exercised the office.
Table row 'Co-rulers': a co-emperor, co-king or co-regent counts only when each exercised the office; a ruling per case.
Table row 'Regents': regency counts only when no monarch reigned on the row in those years.
Table row 'Regents': a regent beside a reigning monarch is not a reign (Galla Placidia: Valentinian III reigned).
Table rows 'Rival claimants' and 'Usurpers': claimant (shown marked, never counts).
Table row 'Exile governments': exile (shown marked); counts only if the row has no occupant at home; a ruling per case.
Task C, v4 rule 4 (RUBRIC8): a reign D11 calls another office, whose lead says the person led or ruled and names the row's own words: de-facto. Beats D11.
Table row 'Another office of the same person': a minister, an ambassador, a seat, a staff post: fix the block, or not a reign if no head-office block exists.
Table row 'Party-states: formal head vs party leader': a party's president, chair or leader is a party office (out) or the de facto leader (shown marked): a ruling per polity phase.
Table row 'Traditional or legendary rulers', read from the evidence record: the lead calls the person legendary or semi-legendary.
The office test: the cited office has a head word and names this row's own state.
Task C, v4 rule 1: D14's office test with a first-five-letters tolerance between the office's words and the row's own words (Tibet / Tibetan); names no other row; D14's guards.

A reign the code decided head whose years overlap another head reign of its row by more than 0 years: a co-ruler, rival or usurper candidate; needs a ruling. Applied in evidence_rules.demote_overlaps after the first pass (a test cannot see the other reigns' verdicts).

The office test read from the evidence record, for a reign the office rule (D14) did not decide (no office text, or one that doesn't name the row): the page is in a category of this row's own monarchs or heads of state, no other status in the categories or the lead, and the reign lies in a phase of the row.

PoC 3: the succession box decides a reign the office text could not: a box about this reign names a head office, the reign's own office text (when it has one) shares a word with it, and the box's predecessor or successor has a reign on the row; no other status in the categories or the lead (acting and provisional are head under definition v3); in a phase of the row.
v4 rule 1: the succession box names an office on head-offices.json (Pope, Manikongo, Hochmeister, King of Kings and 15 more) and the box's neighbour has a reign on the row; the same guards as D14c.
v4 rule 1: the page is in a category of the row's own monarchs or heads of state and the reign lies in the row's years; D14b without the other-row-office guard; the D14c guards.

v4 rule 1: the succession box names a head office that shares a word with the row's own words and the box's neighbour has a reign on the row; D14c without the office-text and other-row guards; a parenthetical box office is skipped.

PoC 2 check: a reign D14 or D14b decided head whose office text or monarchs category names the row's polity with a qualifier (East, West, Upper, Greater...) the row's own words lack. Applied in evidence_rules.demote_checks after the overlap pass; needs a ruling.
